reasoning:
**What is asked.** The ICE BofA US High Yield option-adjusted spread for Friday 4 December 2026, in percentage points, as first published on FRED (series BAMLH0A0HYM2).

**Starting point.** The latest published value is 3.34 for Monday 16 November 2026, up from 3.23 on 13 November and 3.20 on 12 November (FRED). Since the start of October the spread has moved between 3.03 (6 October) and 3.48 (5 November), with 3.44 on 30 October, so it has spent five weeks in a band of roughly 3.1 to 3.5 after widening from 2.66 in late September. Tuesday 17 November is not published yet: the S&P 500 fell 1.0% to a five-month low, the VIX rose to 25.46 and the high-yield funds HYG and JNK lost 0.13% (Closing Look newsletter, 17 November), which points to something near 3.40.

**Time left and width.** Thirteen trading days from the last published value. Daily changes since 1 October have a standard deviation of about 8 basis points, with single days of +18 and -14. A pure random walk would give about 30 basis points by 4 December. The spread has been pulled back toward the middle of its band each time, so I use about 24, with a longer tail on the wide side because spreads jump wider faster than they tighten.

**What is scheduled.** Nvidia's results on 17 November beat forecasts and the shares rose about 3% after hours. Thanksgiving week is usually quiet for credit. The November jobs report lands on 4 December itself, and the Fed meets on 8-9 December with a rate hike more than 90% priced. The 10-year yield is at 5.10%.

**What would move it.** A calmer equity market would take the spread back toward 3.2. A break of the S&P 500's lows or stress among AI-related borrowers could push it past the 5 November high of 3.48, toward 3.8 or more.

**Forecast.** Median 3.36; middle half 3.23 to 3.49; 5th to 95th percentile 3.04 to 3.83, with about 8% above the 3.74 top of the range.
question_title: What will be the ending value of the ICE BofA US High Yield Option-Adjusted Spread for these biweekly periods of Q4 2026? (Nov 23 - Dec 4)
